newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine banks sell T-bills to cut losses.
newsitem.headline: Philippine banks sell T-bills to cut losses.

text.p: Philippine banks are selling their old portfolio of Treasury bills after rates shot up to a two-year high on Monday's auction, traders said on Tuesday.
"Banks would just try to match them with the current rates to get rid of their old inventory," said a foreign bank dealer.
Traders said banks are hurting if they hold on to their T-bills since the Central Bank is borrowing overnight at 32 percent.
"The income from T-bills had been wiped out. And there is the possibility of higher interest rates if the peso remains volatile," another said.
The Central Bank raised its overnight borrowing rate to a 2-1/2 year high last week to 32 percent to fend off speculators.
Traders said buying activity in the market was limited, as banks were just satisfying their clients' requirements.
"Definitely, no one's buying for their positions," the first trader added.
A Reuters poll of four banks gave offers of 12.625/13.75 percent for three-month bills; 13/14.25 percent for six months; and 13.50/15.50 percent for one-year bills.
The average interbank call loan rate slipped to 32.1875 percent from 32.375 percent, with the intra-day high falling to 36 percent from 38 percent.
The market had 33 lenders and 16 borrowers. Volume thinned to 19.11 billion pesos from 31.35 billion.
